note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is not pictured, the redeemer is not pictured, Job is not portrayed as a biblical person but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: Job's friends have shamed him and crushed him with words again and again; whatever his fault, it is his own, and the truth is that God has wronged him and closed his net around him.
ideas: A worn grey-haired man sits on a chair in a bare room with his hands over his ears, while a ring of loudspeaker megaphones on stands all aim at him from close range
In a bare yard three men stand over a worn man on a low stool, all talking down at him at once; he covers his ears with both hands, eyes shut
A blacksmith's hammer comes down again and again on one glowing piece of iron on the anvil
A man bowed under a pile of heavy rolled-up newspapers thrown at him
A man made to stand facing the corner of a room while others lecture his back
A man stands in an open field under a great net that has dropped over him from above and been pegged down all round; he looks up and calls out, and no one is there
A deer stands still in a forest clearing under a wide net that has fallen over it from above, its edges pinned to the ground all round
A small wild bird crouches under a fine net laid over the grass
A fish thrashing in a net drawn tight and lifted from the water
A man with his back to a wall as a heavy curtain of rope netting comes down around him

sections.meaning: Job cries out and gets no answer; God has walled up his road, darkened his way, stripped him of honour, torn up his hope like a tree and surrounded him like an enemy.
ideas: On a country road at dusk a man stands before a tall new brick wall built straight across the road from edge to edge, no way round it, darkness coming on
A man in a long dim tunnel reaches the end and finds it bricked up, the last light behind him going out
A man at a crossroads where every road is closed off by high walls
A man's hand flat against a wall in the dark
A great old tree lies torn out of the ground on a bare hillside, its huge root ball ripped up and lifted into the air
A gardener's empty hole in the soil where a tree was pulled out, its roots lying beside it
A small lone tent at dusk in a valley, ringed on every hillside around it by the lights of a great camp closing in
A trophy cabinet emptied, the shelves bare and dusty outlines where the cups stood
A captain's cap taken off and laid on a table by a man who has lost his ship
A man shouting for help down an empty street with every window shut

sections.meaning: Everyone close to Job has turned away from him: family, friends, servants, his wife, even children; he has become a stranger in his own house.
ideas: A grey-haired man stands in the doorway of his own dining room; his family sit eating and talking at the table and none of them looks up at him, as if he were a stranger
A grey-haired man stands on the step of his own front door; the young woman who opens it looks at him blankly, as at a stranger, holding the door half shut
An old man calls up the stairs of his own house and no one answers
An old married couple lie in bed at night with their backs to each other, the wife turned far away to the very edge, a cold gap between them
In a back yard a close circle of old friends laugh together with their backs turned to one grey-haired man who stands alone at the edge holding a plate
A family photograph on a mantel with one man cut out of it
A small child shrinks behind its mother from a gaunt man who reaches out kindly
A man sits alone at one end of a long family table while everyone has moved their chairs to the other end
A man waves to his brothers across a street and they turn away
A man's coat left on the step outside the closed door of his own house

sections.meaning: Worn to skin and bone, Job begs his friends to pity him, since God's hand has struck him, instead of hounding him as God does.
ideas: A gaunt man, thin as skin and bone in a loose shirt, sits on bare ground holding up both open hands to three friends who stand over him with arms folded, unmoved
A close view of a very thin old hand, skin stretched over bone, held out open and pleading toward three standing men with arms folded, out of focus
A thin man bent over on a bench, his friends standing in a row like judges
A pack of hounds still chasing a deer that can barely stand
A man in a hospital bed reaching for a visitor who steps back
A thin man's reflection in a shop window, his clothes hanging loose
Three friends pressing a man into a corner
A gaunt man holding his hands together pleading
A worn man kneeling in the dust looking up at his friends
A thin wrist with a hospital band, the hand reaching up

sections.meaning: Job wants his words cut into rock forever, because he knows his redeemer lives and will stand at the last, and that he himself, with his own eyes, will see God.
ideas: A close view of a stonemason's hands driving a steel chisel with a hammer into a great face of grey granite, and molten lead being poured into the deep cut grooves
A man's hand writing with a pen in a thick bound book by lamplight
An engraver cutting into a bronze plaque
A cliff face carved with deep, weathered marks that have stood for ages
A worn man sitting on dusty ground among ashes lifts his head with calm certainty toward the first bright light of dawn breaking at the horizon
Over a wide dry plain of dust the first light of morning rises at the horizon and spreads across the ground
A close view of an old man's weathered face, eyes wet and wide open, looking up toward a bright light with longing and certainty
A frail, gaunt old man in a hospital bed turns his face toward a window where bright morning light pours in, his face lit with longing
A man on a ship's deck sees the lighthouse light come up out of the dark
A watchman on a wall sees the dawn

sections.meaning: Those who hound Job and blame him should fear judgment themselves, for there is a judgment.
ideas: A close view of a man's hand pointing an accusing finger forward, while its other three fingers curl back to point at his own chest
Three men point at a seated man while behind them a great dark storm front rolls in over the hills toward them
A judge's gavel resting on a bench
Balance scales tipping
A sword hanging by a thread over the heads of three men
A lightning bolt striking near three accusers
A man throwing stones that bounce back at him
A boomerang returning to the thrower
A mirror held up to the accusers
Clouds gathering over a house where three men stand pointing

candidates.prompt: In a bare room with pale walls in plain daylight, a worn grey-haired man in a plain shirt sits on a wooden chair, hunched, pressing both hands over his ears, eyes shut tight in pain. All round him, very close, a ring of big old loudspeaker megaphones on metal stands are aimed straight at his head from every side. The man and the megaphones are in the upper middle of the picture; below is only the bare wooden floor.

In a bare dusty yard on a grey afternoon, a worn grey-haired man in a plain shirt sits on a low wooden stool, pressing both hands over his ears, eyes shut, worn out. Three men in everyday clothes stand close over him, all leaning down and talking at him at once, one jabbing a finger, one counting points off on his fingers. Their heads and the man's face are in the upper part of the picture.

In an open grassy field under a wide pale sky, a man in plain everyday clothes stands caught under a great rope net that has been thrown over him from above; its edges are pegged down into the ground all round him. He has his hands up gripping the mesh and his face lifted, calling out for help, and there is no one anywhere in sight. The man and the net are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

In a quiet forest clearing in soft daylight, a young deer stands still under a wide hunting net that has fallen over it from above; the net's edges are pinned to the ground all round it and the mesh lies over its back and head. It looks out through the mesh, unable to get free. No hunter is anywhere in sight.

Seen from behind, a man in a plain jacket stands on a narrow country road at dusk. Right in front of him a tall new brick wall has been built straight across the road from one side to the other, higher than his head, with thick hedges and rock on both sides, so there is no way past. The light is fading and darkness is coming on over the road ahead. The man and the wall are in the upper two thirds of the picture; below is only the empty road surface.

Seen from behind, a man in a plain jacket stands at the far end of a long, dim stone tunnel, facing a solid wall of new bricks that blocks it completely from floor to roof. His hand rests flat against the bricks. Behind him the faint light from the tunnel's entrance is fading into darkness. The man and the brick wall are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A great old oak tree lies torn out of the ground on a bare hillside after a storm. Its whole huge root ball has been ripped up out of the earth and stands up on end in the air, roots dangling with soil, beside the deep raw hole where it grew. Its trunk and branches lie flat across the grass. Grey sky with breaking clouds.

Seen from a hilltop at deep blue dusk, one small lone tent stands in the middle of a wide bare valley, a faint lamp glowing inside it. On every hillside all round it, in a complete closed ring, hundreds of camp fires and lit tents of a great camp have been set up, hemming it in on every side.

In a warm, lamplit family dining room in the evening, a long table is full of a family of every age eating and talking happily. A worn grey-haired man in a plain cardigan stands just inside the doorway of the room, looking at them, his hand on the door frame. None of them looks up at him; they look past him as if he were a stranger. The table and the man are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

At the front door of a family house on a grey afternoon, a worn grey-haired man in a plain coat stands on the step. The door has been opened only a little by a younger woman of the household, who looks at him blankly and coldly, as at a stranger, holding the door half shut against him. Behind her the warm hallway of the house he once lived in. Both faces are in the upper part of the picture.

In a sunny back yard at a summer gathering, a close circle of men and women laugh and talk together with their backs turned to one grey-haired man, who stands alone at the edge of the lawn holding a paper plate, looking at them. Not one of them turns toward him. Everyone is in the upper two thirds of the picture; below is only lawn.

In a dim bedroom at night, lit by a little light from the hall, an older married couple lie in a wide bed with their backs to each other. The wife has turned away to the very edge of her side, her face toward the wall, and a wide cold gap of empty sheet lies between them. The grey-haired husband lies awake looking at her back. The heads and pillows are in the upper half of the picture.

On bare dusty ground outside a house on a grey day, a gaunt man worn thin to skin and bone, in a loose plain shirt hanging off his shoulders, sits looking up and holding out both open hands, begging for pity. Three friends in everyday clothes stand over him with their arms folded, unmoved, looking down at him. Their faces and his are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A close view of a very thin old hand and wrist, the skin stretched tight over the bones, held out open and palm up, pleading. Beyond it, slightly out of focus, three men stand side by side with their arms folded, unmoved. Soft grey daylight. The hand and the three men are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A close view of a stonemason's strong hands driving a steel chisel with a hammer into the smooth face of a huge grey granite boulder, chips of stone flying. Along the rock run deep cut grooves, and a thin stream of bright molten lead is being poured from a small iron ladle into them, filling them. The grooves are plain straight lines seen at a low angle, not letters or marks that can be read. Clear daylight. The hands and chisel are in the upper middle of the picture.

By the light of a lamp at a plain wooden desk at night, a worn grey-haired man's hand writes carefully with a fountain pen in a thick, heavy bound book lying open. The writing is far too small and soft in focus to read. His other hand holds the page flat. The hand, pen and book are in the upper middle of the picture.

A worn, thin man in a plain shirt sits on dry dusty ground among grey ashes and broken things, at the very first light of morning. He has lifted his head and looks out with calm, sure hope toward the horizon, where bright golden dawn light is breaking and rising over the dust. The man and the dawn are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A wide, flat plain of dry grey dust and ash stretches away under a dark sky at the very end of night. At the horizon the first bright light of dawn is rising, and long golden rays are spreading out over the dust toward the viewer.

A close portrait of an old, gaunt man's weathered face, lit by a soft bright light from above. His eyes are wide open and wet with tears, gazing upward with deep longing and complete certainty, as if he is about to see what he has waited for all his life. His eyes are in the upper half of the picture.

A frail, gaunt old man lies propped up in a plain bed in a simple room, his body worn out. He has turned his face toward a tall window where bright, clear morning light is pouring in, and his face is lit with longing and sure hope, eyes wide open. The man's face and the window are in the upper two thirds of the picture.

A close view of a man's hand pointing an accusing finger forward, while its other three fingers are curled back, pointing at the man's own chest. His shirt and shoulder are behind it, slightly out of focus. Plain daylight. The hand is in the upper middle of the picture.

On an open hillside, three men in everyday clothes stand pointing accusingly at a worn man who sits on the ground before them. Behind the three men, unseen by them, a huge dark storm front is rolling in over the hills toward them, black clouds low and heavy. The men and the storm are in the upper two thirds of the picture.
